audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows contradicted the whys sitting next to them. Level 1 read Mordekaiser while whys[0] says Gnar throws boomerangs at you for free; Levels 2 and 3 read Skill/Gnar while whys[1] and whys[2] say your Q+W and the E-pull beat squishy mini form; First item read Gnar while whys[5] says it hinges on his Rage bar.
audit.why: The packet chart reads Gnar / Mordekaiser / Mordekaiser / Gnar / Mordekaiser / Skill / Gnar and the mirror has already flipped the whole chart to it. The prose was right and only the side tokens were wrong.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2 and 5 flipped as one atomic group in both layers with ratings realigned to the inverse of the mirror's (Gnar rows 4/10 ours, Mordekaiser rows 7/10, Skill 5/10). phases[3].why and phases[5].why rewritten so the reason matches the side.

audit.why: The spike list is unusually good already — it uses 'Full Rage' as a spike rather than a level, which is the right axis for Gnar, and the level 6 and 2+ item spikes are accurate.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags it directly: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere, 0 sequencing cues. Every reference to GNAR! said 'his Mega all-in, don't fight transform' with no number, and Hop and Wallop were never given cooldowns at all.
audit.why: GNAR! is 90/60/30, Hop/Crunch is 22/19.5/17/14.5/12 and Wallop is a flat 7 — those are the numbers that turn 'don't fight transform' into a real window. The wall interaction also matters: Riot's R text stuns and adds bonus damage only when an enemy hits a wall, so open ground is a decision you make, not luck.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].d and phases[3].why; the wall clause stated as the reason to fight in open ground.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Track GNAR! before every engage' treated a 90-second ultimate the same as a basic ability.
audit.why: A spent GNAR! at rank 1 is a full minute and a half of safety — the single most punishable cooldown in the matchup and it had no duration attached.
audit.corrected: Stated as 90s at rank 1 with the window named, in dosFull[0].d.

edits.before: Q ranks make isolated hits massive. Gnar must hug minions all lane; punish every step away from the wave with the full drag combo.
edits.after: Q ranks hit hard, but Boomerang Throw is 16s at rank 1 and slows you the whole way in — he chips and hops out unless the wave holds him.

edits.before: Liandry's makes Darkness Rise melt through bruiser HP stacking. Extended trades are now strictly yours — force them.
edits.after: Liandry's burns him down in mini form, but a full Rage bar and one Wallop stun flips the same trade — check the bar first.

edits.before: - Gnar GNAR! (Mega Stun): matchup-defining — His Mega all-in. Don’t fight transform. Track it before every engage. - Gnar GNAR!: Mega only: knocks up + slows; against a wall it stuns long. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - GNAR! (R): 90/60/30s — Mega only, and a wall turns the knockback into a long stun, so fight in open ground. - Hop/Crunch (E): 22s at rank 1, his only escape. - Wallop (W): 7s, the Mega stun that flips your all-in.

edits.before: His Mega all-in. Don’t fight transform. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: GNAR! is 90s at rank 1 — after he spends it, you own the next full minute.

edits.after: Mega Gnar is a different champion — wait out the form, it is a timer not a choice.

edits.after: Realm of Death is 650 range on a 140s timer — do not whiff it kiting.

notes: No suspect names in this packet. Agreeing with the mirror agent: the Mordekaiser kit file tags 'grounding' on Obliterate (Q) but Riot's Q text says nothing of the kind, so I asserted no dash-denial against Hop anywhere — that would be the single most tempting fabrication in this matchup and it is not supported. The Rage bar is the real tracked resource here rather than a cooldown, and the page already handles that correctly in spikes[2] ('Full Rage' as the spike); I left that framing alone.
